_comment: Hand-authored mapping of each Material Web component (custom element) to the OpenUI scope tree. {{Name}} is resolved to a link by tools/build_reports.py. match is one of: Exact, Alias, Narrower, Broader, Related, Gap. image is a path under docs/components/images/ of the material-web checkout.

components.name: Elevated button
components.alias: {{Action controls}} scope; entry {{Button}}. Emphasis (elevated, filled, filled tonal, outlined, text) is a design-system variant; Action controls declares no variant attribute. Presentation: {{Elevation}}.
components.description: A filled tonal button with a shadow, for a button that needs visual separation from a patterned background. Use sparingly to avoid shadow creep. It has label text and an optional icon (`icon` slot, `trailing-icon`); with `href` it acts as a link, otherwise as a form button (`type` submit, reset or button, with `name` and `value`). `disabled` removes it from the tab order, `soft-disabled` keeps it focusable.

components.name: Filled button
components.alias: {{Action controls}} scope; entry {{Button}}. High-emphasis variant; same gap as the elevated button.
components.description: The highest-emphasis button after the FAB. Use it for important, final actions that complete a flow, such as Save, Join now or Confirm. Same properties as every Material Web button.

components.name: Filled tonal button
components.alias: {{Action controls}} scope; entry {{Button}}. Medium-emphasis variant.
components.description: A middle ground between filled and outlined buttons, for a lower-priority button that needs slightly more emphasis than an outline gives, such as Next in an onboarding flow.

components.name: Outlined button
components.alias: {{Action controls}} scope; entry {{Button}}. Medium-emphasis variant.
components.description: A medium-emphasis button for actions that are important but not the primary action of the app.

components.name: Text button
components.alias: {{Action controls}} scope; entry {{Button}}. Lowest-emphasis variant.
components.description: The lowest-priority button, used especially when presenting several options side by side.

components.name: Checkbox
components.alias: {{Checkbox}} in {{Choice controls}}: `uses.checked`, `uses.indeterminate`, `uses.required`, `produces.selectionChange`. Match is complete.
components.description: Lets users select one or more items from a set, or turn an option on or off. It is standalone, pre-checked or indeterminate. It is form-associated (`checked`, `indeterminate`, `required`, `value`, `name`, `disabled`), emits `change` and `input`, and has the constraint-validation methods. Labels come from a `<label>` element, but the doc says a checkbox always needs an `aria-label`.

components.name: Chip set
components.alias: {{Token collection}} and {{Editable chip collection}} (A20, A21; {{List}} scope). Its ARIA role is `toolbar`, so also {{Toolbar}}. No Chip term exists.
components.description: The container that chips should always appear in. A chip set is a toolbar that can hold any type of chip or other toolbar items, and it handles keyboard focus between them. Label it with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

components.name: Assist chip
components.alias: {{Button}} ({{Action controls}}). Closest command surface; the chip's compact, dynamic and contextual appearance has no term.
components.description: Represents a smart or automated action that can span several apps, such as opening a calendar event from the home screen. It works as though the user asked an assistant to do it, and should appear dynamically and contextually. Optional `elevated`, optional icon, and `href` to act as a link.

components.name: Filter chip
components.alias: {{Toggle button}} ({{Action controls}}, `uses.pressed`), the doc itself calls chips 'a good alternative to toggle buttons or checkboxes'. Also {{Checkbox}}.
components.description: Uses tags or descriptive words to filter content. It has a `selected` state with an optional selected icon (`has-selected-icon`), can be `removable` (trailing remove icon) and `elevated`, and emits `remove`.

components.name: Input chip
components.alias: An item of a {{Token collection}} or {{Editable chip collection}} ({{List}} scope, A20 and A21).
components.description: A discrete piece of information entered by the user, such as a Gmail contact or a filter option inside a search field. All input chips are removable; one with no click action is `remove-only`. With `avatar`, a user image shows in a larger circle.

components.name: Suggestion chip
components.alias: {{Text completion}} ({{Input assistance}}) names the behavior of offering suggestions; the chip is its control, a {{Button}}.
components.description: Narrows the user's intent with dynamically generated suggestions, such as possible replies or search filters. Optional `elevated`, optional icon, `href` for link behavior.

components.name: Dialog
components.alias: {{Dialog}} (glossary, {{Dialog scope|Widgets/dialog}}): `uses.open`, `uses.modal`, `produces.close`, `produces.cancel`. Its modal behavior is {{Modal overlay}}. `type="alert"` is `role=alertdialog`.
components.description: Provides important prompts in a user flow. It behaves like a `<dialog>` element and can be closed with a `<form method="dialog">`. It has three optional sections: headline, content and actions (slots `headline`, `content`, `actions`). It opens and closes through `open`, `show()` and `close()` (both return a Promise), and a button's `value` sets `returnValue`. Events: `open`, `opened`, `close`, `closed`, `cancel`. `type="alert"` marks an important message that needs a response.

components.name: Divider
components.alias: {{Divider}}, alias of {{Separator}} ({{Display primitives}}: `uses.decorative`, `uses.orientation`). Gap: the inset variants.
components.description: A thin line that groups content in lists and containers. Full-width dividers separate larger sections of unrelated content; inset dividers (`inset`, `inset-start`, `inset-end`) separate related content within a section. Decorative by default; give a non-decorative divider `role="separator"` so it is announced.

components.name: Elevation
components.alias: {{Elevation}} and {{Shadow}} ({{Presentation}} scope, folder abstraction; R8: elevation is a depth level that may be drawn as a shadow).
components.description: The relative distance between two surfaces along the z-axis. The level is 0 to 5 through `--md-elevation-level`; resting states use 0 to +3 and +4 and +5 are reserved for user-interacted states such as hover and dragged. The element fills the nearest `position: relative` element's size and shape, and can be animated between levels. It is visual only and has no accessibility requirements.

components.name: Floating action button (FAB)
components.alias: {{Button}} (glossary aliases 'floating action button' and 'FAB'). The glossary calls it 'a design-system variant, not a separate semantic primitive'.
components.description: The most important action on a screen, kept within reach. It shows an icon (an `md-icon`, an `svg` or an `img`). `variant` is surface (default), primary, secondary or tertiary; `size` is small, medium (default) or large; `lowered` sets a lower elevation. With `label` it becomes an extended FAB, the only FAB that may omit its icon.

components.name: Branded FAB
components.alias: {{Button}} (FAB variant). Gap: a brand-logo icon is not modeled.
components.description: A FAB whose icon is a brightly colored logo. Unlike a standard FAB it has no color variants, always shows its logo, and comes in medium (default) or large; with `label` it extends.

components.name: Focus ring
components.alias: {{Focus outline}} (A66, {{Presentation}}); the focus itself is the {{Focus state}} (Interaction).
components.description: An accessible outline that shows keyboard focus, following the `:focus-visible` heuristics. It attaches to the parent element, to a referenced element (`for`) or imperatively, and must sit in a `position: relative` container. `inward` animates it inward, which suits list items. Its animation can be changed or disabled with CSS custom properties. It is visual only.

components.name: Icon button
components.alias: {{Icon button}} (alias of {{Button}}; {{Action controls}}). With `toggle` it is a {{Toggle button}} (`selected` is `uses.pressed`).
components.description: The standard icon button has no background or outline and the lowest emphasis. Icon buttons give supplementary actions in a compact layout: opening an overflow menu or search, or binary actions such as favorite or bookmark. `toggle` and `selected` make a toggle button, with a second icon in `slot="selected"` and an `aria-label-selected`. `href` turns it into a link. `flip-icon-in-rtl` mirrors the icon in right-to-left layouts.

components.name: Filled icon button
components.alias: {{Icon button}} ({{Action controls}}). High-emphasis variant.
components.description: A circular icon button with higher visual impact, best for high-emphasis actions.

components.name: Filled tonal icon button
components.alias: {{Icon button}} ({{Action controls}}). Medium-emphasis variant.
components.description: A middle ground between the filled and outlined icon buttons, for a button that needs slightly more emphasis than an outline, such as a secondary action next to a high-emphasis one.

components.name: Outlined icon button
components.alias: {{Icon button}} ({{Action controls}}). Medium-emphasis variant.
components.description: A medium-emphasis icon button, for when a button needs more emphasis than a standard icon button but less than a filled or filled tonal one.

components.name: Icon
components.alias: {{Icon}} ({{Display primitives}}: `uses.src`, `uses.alt`, `uses.decorative`); the icon system is {{Iconography}} ({{Presentation}}).
components.description: Shows an icon by name (ligature), by Unicode code point or as an `<svg>` child. The Material Symbols font has three styles (outlined, rounded, sharp) and four variable axes: weight, fill, grade and optical size; `fill` and `grade` are set through `font-variation-settings`. Icons used on their own need an accessible name when they are focusable.

components.name: List
components.alias: {{List}} ({{List}} scope: `uses.selection`, child `listItem`).
components.description: A continuous, vertical index of text and images. `<md-list>` is a container of `<md-list-item>` elements of different types. It sets `role="list"` and `tabindex="-1"` by default and has `activateNextItem()` and `activatePreviousItem()` for keyboard navigation.

components.name: List item
components.alias: The `listItem` child of {{List}} ({{List}} scope). Interactive types map to {{Link|Link term}} (`type=link`) or {{Button}} (`type=button`).
components.description: One item of a list: a headline, optional supporting and trailing supporting text, and optional icon, avatar or image slots (`start`, `end`). `type` is text (default), link or button; `href` and `target` apply to a link. `role="listitem"` and `tabindex="0"` by default; the allowed `type` values are limited to keep lists accessible.

components.name: Menu
components.alias: {{Menu}} ({{Menu widgets}}: `uses.open`, `uses.anchor`, `produces.select`). The anchor and its button together are a {{Menu button}}.
components.description: Displays a list of choices on a temporary surface. It positions itself against an `anchor` or `anchorElement` and renders `md-menu-item` children, handles keyboard navigation and typeahead, and reports how it closed through the `close-menu` event. `positioning` is absolute (default), fixed, document or popover (uses the top layer). Events: `opening`, `opened`, `closing`, `closed`.

components.name: Menu item
components.alias: {{Menu item}} (`menuitem` child of {{Menu widgets}}).
components.description: One command or choice of a menu: a headline with optional supporting text and start or end slots. `type` sets its behavior and role (default `menuitem`), `keep-open` leaves the menu open after a choice, and `selected` and `disabled` set state.

components.name: Sub menu
components.alias: The `submenu` child of {{Menu widgets}} (nested menu).
components.description: A menu item that opens a nested `md-menu` from its `menu` slot. The root menu needs `has-overflow` to show nested menus. Open and close on hover are delayed by `hover-open-delay` and `hover-close-delay`.

components.name: Linear progress
components.alias: {{Progress bar}} ({{Status indicator}}: `uses.value`, `uses.max`, `uses.mode`). Gap: the `buffer` display.
components.description: Shows progress along a fixed, visible track. It is determinate (`value` and `max`) or `indeterminate`. `buffer` shows known progress as the bar and track and unknown progress as buffer dots. `four-color` cycles the indeterminate color through primary, primary container, tertiary and tertiary container. Needs an `aria-label`.

components.name: Circular progress
components.alias: {{Spinner}} and {{Loader}} ({{Status indicator}}), with {{Progress mode}} for determinate or indeterminate.
components.description: Shows progress by animating clockwise along an invisible circular track. Determinate (`value`, `max`) or `indeterminate`; `four-color` as for linear progress. Needs an `aria-label`.

components.name: Radio button
components.alias: {{Radio button}} ({{Choice controls}}); the group is {{Exclusive selection coordination}} (`role=radiogroup`).
components.description: Lets people select one option from a set. It behaves like `<input type="radio">`: radios with the same `name` form a group and only one is selected. `checked`, `value` and `required`; events `input` and `change`. Place radios in a `role="radiogroup"` with a label; do not wrap a radio in a `<label>`, and give each an `aria-label`.

components.name: Ripple
components.alias: {{Visual states}} ({{Presentation}}) with {{Hover state}} and {{Pressed state}} (Interaction). The Presentation scope names the ripple as presentation but no term exists; candidate new term: State layer.
components.description: A state layer: a semi-transparent covering on an element that shows its state, on hover and press pointer interactions. It can cover the whole element (bounded) or be a circle centered on it (unbounded). It attaches to the parent, to a referenced element (`for`) or imperatively. Visual only.

components.name: Filled select
components.alias: {{Dropdown}} ({{Choice controls}}; M3 also calls it a dropdown menu). Single choice only: {{Selection mode}} has no multiple counterpart here. `label`, `supporting-text` and `error-text` are {{Form field}} (A44) concerns.
components.description: Lets users choose one value from a fixed list of options and shows the chosen option above the menu. Like the native `<select>`. `value`, `selected-index`, `required`, `label`, `supporting-text`, `error-text`, `has-leading-icon`, `menu-positioning`. Events: `change`, `input`, `opening`, `opened`, `closing`, `closed`. Filled style.

components.name: Outlined select
components.alias: {{Dropdown}} ({{Choice controls}}). Same as the filled select.
components.description: The same component and API as the filled select, drawn with an outline.

components.name: Select option
components.alias: The option of a {{Dropdown}} or {{List box}} (HTML `option`). No separate OpenUI term.
components.description: One option of a select, with a form `value` and `selected` and `disabled` states. Events: `close-menu`, `request-selection`, `request-deselection`.

components.name: Slider
components.alias: {{Slider}} ({{Range control}}: `uses.value`, `uses.min`, `uses.max`, `uses.step`); with `range`, the {{Range slider}} (`uses.start`, `uses.end`). Gap: the value label and tick marks.
components.description: Lets users view and select a value, or a range, along a track, such as volume or brightness. It is continuous or discrete (`step` with `ticks`), and with `range` has two handles (`value-start`, `value-end`). `labeled` shows a value label on the selected handle. Events: `change`, `input`.

components.name: Switch
components.alias: {{Switch}} ({{Choice controls}}: `uses.checked`).
components.description: Toggles the state of an item on or off. It is similar to a checkbox and is `selected` or not. `icons` and `show-only-selected-icon` add icons that emphasize the selected state. Form-associated with `value`, `name` and `required`; events `input` and `change`. Needs an `aria-label`.

components.name: Tabs
components.alias: {{Tab}} and {{Tab Bar}} ({{Tabs}} scope: `uses.selectedIndex`, `produces.selectedTabChange`).
components.description: Organizes groups of related content at the same level of hierarchy. A tab bar holds several primary or secondary tabs and should not mix the two. `active-tab-index` selects a tab, `auto-activate` selects on focus, `scrollToTab()` scrolls a long bar, and the `change` event reports a new selection. Every tab references a `role="tabpanel"` through `aria-controls`.

components.name: Primary tab
components.alias: The `tab` child of {{Tabs}} ({{Tabs}} scope). The primary or secondary level is not modeled.
components.description: Placed at the top of the content pane under a top app bar to show the main content destinations. The icon sits above the label, or inline with `inline-icon`; `icon-only` marks a tab that has only an icon.

components.name: Secondary tab
components.alias: The `tab` child of {{Tabs}} ({{Tabs}} scope). The primary or secondary level is not modeled.
components.description: Used inside a content area to separate related content further and set up a hierarchy. Its icon is inline with the label.

components.name: Filled text field
components.alias: {{Text field}} ({{Text inputs}}: `uses.type`, `uses.multiline`, `uses.maxLength`, `uses.placeholder`, `uses.required`, `uses.readOnly`, `produces.valueChange`). Gaps: prefix and suffix text, supporting and error text, character counter, leading and trailing icons, number type (OpenUI uses {{Step input}}).
components.description: Lets users enter text. It behaves like `<input>`; `type` is text (default), email, number, password, search, tel, url or textarea (multi-line, with `rows`). The label floats, is a placeholder or is external. `prefix-text`, `suffix-text`, `supporting-text` (replaced by `error-text` when invalid), a character counter with `maxlength`, and leading and trailing icons. Validation uses the browser constraint-validation API or manual `error`.

components.name: Outlined text field
components.alias: {{Text field}} ({{Text inputs}}). Same as the filled text field.
components.description: The same component and API as the filled text field, drawn with an outline.
